  • The difference between Graph and Runtime

The difference between Graph and Runtime

ATOM SDK has two ways to operate the graph: Graph mode (editing state) and Runtime mode (executing state). Their interfaces are different and their applicable scenarios are also different.

Core differences

Dimension Graph Mode Runtime Mode

Main purpose

Edit graph structure and debug nodes

runs the graph as an execution engine

uses Service

GraphService、NodeService、GraphNodeService

RuntimeService

Open with

client.graph.open_graph("my_graph")

client.runtime.load_graph("my_graph")

Parameter settings

Set one by one by node ID

Batch settings by binding name

Input data

Read/set port data

Normal mode sending RuntimeFrame; Passive binocular mode sending EPICRAW3

Whether to carry timestamp

Yes (versioning required for editing operations)

No

Graph mode: for editing

Use the Graph pattern when you need to build or modify a graph structure:

  • Create new graph, open graph, run graph, release graph, query graph list

  • Create, delete, copy nodes

  • Connect and disconnect node ports

  • Set node parameters (init_params, run_params)

  • Upload model file

  • Read node output data

from pathlib import Path
from atom_sdk import CreateNodeParams, NodeParamUpdate, RuntimeFrame, RuntimeRunParams

# Graph Pattern example:Create a graph and configure nodes
client = AtomClient("http://127.0.0.1:10026")

# Open the image and enter editing mode
client.graph.open_graph("detection_graph")

# Create node
result = client.node.create_node(CreateNodeParams("detection_graph", "DetectorNode"))
print("Create node request status:", result["status"])
node_id = result["nodeId"]

# Set parameters
client.node.set_node_param_data(
    NodeParamUpdate(
        "detection_graph", node_id, "model_path", "init_params",
        Path("/models/detector.bin"),
    )
)

# Run chart
run_result = client.graph.run_graph("detection_graph")
print("Run request status:", run_result["status"])

Runtime mode: used for execution

When you need to use Atom as an execution engine, use Runtime mode:

  • The picture has been designed on the Atom front-end and the parameters have been configured.

  • In normal mode, your program takes one frame (or multiple frames) of image + point cloud each time and sends it to Atom for execution.

  • In passive binocular passive_bino mode, your program sends complete EPICRAW3 raw data

  • Get the execution results (detection frames, grab points, etc.)

When using runtime.run_graph, the current version requires that there are EpicPro输入 or EpicPro输入(单组数据) nodes and EpicPro输出 nodes in the graph. Otherwise, it cannot run and an error will be reported.

 
# Runtime Pattern example:The picture is ready,Only responsible for execution
client = AtomClient("http://127.0.0.1:10026")

# Load graph(Not an editor,Is execution state initialization)
load_result = client.runtime.load_graph("detection_graph")
print("Load request status:", load_result["status"])

# Normal mode:Package already exists EPICRAW,or use from_data Generate locally
frame = RuntimeFrame.from_file(
    "frame.epicraw",
    cam2_base=[x, y, z, rx, ry, rz],  # Rotate vector form,The length is 6
)
result = client.runtime.run_graph(RuntimeRunParams("detection_graph", [frame]))
print("Run request status:", result["status"])

print(result["instanceList"])

If EpicProInput in the picture is configured as passive_bino, do not use RuntimeFrame above. Please use RuntimeRunParams.passive_bino_from_file(…​) or RuntimeRunParams.passive_bino_from_images(…​) to pass EPICRAW3 instead. See Runtime input frames (RuntimeFrame / RuntimePassiveBinoFrame) for details.

Can the same picture be used in both modes at the same time?

Not recommended, but technically possible. Graph mode will modify the graph structure, which may lead to unexpected results when executed concurrently with Runtime.

Recommended methods in actual projects:

  1. Development phase: Editing and debugging graphs in Graph mode

  2. Production phase: Fixed graph structure, only executed in Runtime mode

Why does RuntimeService have its own list_graphs and get_all_nodes_info?

These methods of the Runtime interface return "runtime visible" graphs and nodes, which may be different from the edit state view (for example, some nodes are filtered out in runtime mode). The two are also independent on the API route (/Runtime/ vs /Graph/).

Common misunderstandings

Myth 1: run_graph in Graph mode and run_graph in Runtime mode are the same

Both can run graphs, but the mechanisms are different:

  • GraphService.run_graph: Run in edit mode, requires timestamp, suitable for debugging

  • RuntimeService.run_graph: Accepts multi-frame input, sends binary data, and returns structured inference results

When using RuntimeService.run_graph, the current version requires that there are EpicPro输入 or EpicPro输入(单组数据) nodes and EpicPro输出 nodes in the graph. Otherwise, it cannot run and an error will be reported.

Myth 2: You must first open_graph and then runtime.load_graph

The two are independent: open_graph enters the editing state, and load_graph enters the runtime state. There is no need to execute the former before the latter.
